sense: going by: walk past, go past

evidence: Caes. BG 1.48.2: praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit
terms.comment: Past a thing, going by it: praeter castra, past the camp. For “except”, see except.

terms.grammar: verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative
evidence: Plaut. Aul. 474: jam hunc nōn ausim praeterīre
terms.comment: Latin usually says “go past” with one verb: praeterīre, go past; praetervolāre, fly past; praeterfluere, flow past; praetervehī, sail or drive past.

phrases.latin: Postrīdiē ejus diēī praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit
phrases.english: the next day he led his forces past Caesar’s camp

phrases.latin: dum haec putō, praeteriī imprūdēns vīllam: longē jam abieram cum sēnsī
phrases.english: while I was thinking this over I went past the house without noticing; I had gone a long way before I realised

phrases.latin: jam hunc nōn ausim praeterīre, quīn cōnsistam et conloquar
phrases.english: I wouldn’t dare go past him now without stopping for a word

phrases.latin: facilius tamen īnsīdit quod exspectātur quam quod praetervolat
phrases.english: still, what is waited for sinks in more easily than what flies past

sources: Lewis & Short: praeter · Lewis & Short: praetereo
